reviews.title: Outstanding Airflow, Smart Design, and Premium Feel for the Price
reviews.comment:
. If you’re on the fence, this is one of those cases that’s easy to recommend and easy to upvote.
Build quality:
As expected from Lian Li, the materials feel solid and well-finished. No sharp edges, no flimsy panels, and the steel frame feels sturdy without being overly heavy. The side panel fits perfectly and doesn’t flex or rattle.
Airflow & thermals:
This case absolutely nails airflow. The mesh front is wide open without looking cheap, and airflow-focused layouts clearly drove the design. My CPU and GPU temps dropped noticeably compared to my previous case, even under load. You can tell this was designed by people who actually care about cooling.
Layout & ease of building:
Cable management is straightforward and forgiving, even if you’re not a perfectionist. There’s plenty of room behind the motherboard tray, sensible routing holes, and good clearance for modern GPUs and air coolers. Everything just makes sense when you’re building in it.
Looks:
Clean, modern, and not overdone. It looks great on a desk without screaming “RGB gamer box,” but still gives you plenty of room to show off components if that’s your thing.
Value:
For the price, this case punches way above its weight. You’re getting Lian Li quality, excellent airflow, and a builder-friendly layout without paying a premium.
Final thoughts:
If you want a case that’s easy to build in, keeps components cool, and looks great. One thing to add is I wouldn’t recommend if you are moving your PC around a lot as it’s all snap in panels.
reviews.author: Jesse

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment:
I got this case to transfer my build from a less desirable one. Building in this case is very easy! The cable management can take a bit of finagling, but it can be done and look well. It's a solid and while compact, does still provide plenty of room to work with. I like the simple, clean looks of the case.
The only thing I'm not a fan of is the included front fans (not enough to remove a star). They can be a bit noisy/resonant on the case. I've read that tuning fan curves helps. Ultimately, I installed rubber/silicone gaskets between the case and front fans and the fans are quiet again.

reviews.title: Budget Case that feels premium!
reviews.comment:
A sleek and modern case with excellent airflow. Feels premium too!
Important Details:
- Cable management is a little tight but not impossible!
- Stock fans aren't silent, but they aren't loud by any means. Either way, 4 free fans is a steal, and you can always upgrade them later on!
- I would say OpenRGB is the best software to mess around with the RGB fans on the front.

reviews.title: Great Case, Minor Flaws
reviews.comment:
Saw this a few times on Gamer's Nexus and got it based on their reviews
Pros:
+ Looks great
+ Cheap price
+ Cools well
+ Lots of room despite small size
+ Easy to install everything
+ Easy to remove and clean filters/mesh
- Fans have annoying humming noticeable when room is quiet
- GPU makes contact with case near front of case
- Not a lot of room on the side for cable management. Recommend flat cables
- No reset button ,only power button
- No filter for bottom back intake
~ LED fans cannot be manged in Linux
reviews.author: Brandon Nass

reviews.title: The perfect pc case (w/ room for improvements)
reviews.comment:
This is an amazing case.
1. Airflow is just perfect, at most you'll need 3 additional fans for exhaust, no need for to buy extra intake fans.
2. RGB looks good and can be disabled if wanted for stealth look.
3. It has built in GPU Support bracket to avoid sag.
4. Opening/Closing is really well design, building a pc is a delight as well as changing components.
5. Front USB-C is a nice detail.
6. Enough space for large gpu and cpu cooling
7. The best case on it's price range.
Cons:
1. Due to the placement of the PSU, you might need a modular power supply.
2. Manually switching the PSU requires screwing (fortunately it's a easy screw by hand).
3. Cable management could be difficult on complex builds (RGA controllers, etc). For simple builds this is not a real issue imo.
4. Power supply air intake could have a bit more room.
5. Graphics card intake doesn't have a filter, could led to pet hair / more dust getting into the system. (easily fixable by using a DIY PC Case Dust Mesh Filter).
